title: HD26 Supper: Food-Specific Attack Rates as of 10:35

fields.heading: HD26 Supper — Food-Specific Attack Rates, Interviewed Attendees as of 10:35, Mon 10/12/2026 (22 ill, 31 well; ill = probable or suspect, onset after the meal)
fields.source: HD26 coded line list and standard questionnaire food histories (yes/no per dish), 53 interviewed attendees of the Heritage Days Supper, Sat 10/10/2026. Tabulated by D. Kulkarni, MCHD backup data analyst, 10:42. Crude 2x2 per item only; stratified analysis not run.

data.title: Food-specific attack rates, crude (n = 53: 22 ill, 31 well)
notes: AR = attack rate (ill / total in group). RR = AR ate / AR did not eat. OR = (ill ate x well did not eat) / (ill did not eat x well ate).
Two of the 24 coded cases (as of 10:35) not yet interviewed; not included.

Handwritten, D.K.: 17 of the 19 ill coleslaw eaters also ate the pasta salad. They sat side by side on the buffet, same Kessler tubs. I can't separate them with this n. Stratified run not done. Chicken: Prairie Table's own kitchen, and the 06/2026 cold-holding finding. Senior meal prep starts 18:00.

instructorNote: This is the decision point. The table points to the two Kessler salads but can't tell them apart, and the chicken signal is weaker but still there. Before the 18:00 prep, the Director, advised by the EHS, should pick and log one option in the decision log (MOISOP §8): a documented voluntary hold plus a request to pause or modify the senior meal, a signed embargo, or a closure. The log entry should record the facts known, the option chosen and the reason. Watch for the Epi Lead to say the stratified analysis is still pending and to keep any vehicle name out of public messaging.
